definitions.definition: (transitive) To leave or withdraw from; to quit; to retire from

quote.citation: 1757, Edmund Burke, The Abridgement of the History of England:
quote.text: The Norwegians were forced to evacuate the country.

definitions.definition: To cause (or help) to leave or withdraw from.

quote.citation: 1943 November and December, G. T. Porter, “The Lines Behind the Lines in Burma”, in Railway Magazine, page 327:
quote.text: Early the next morning I set off on the long and hazardous trek through jungles and hills into Assam, and regretfully said "good-bye" to the gallant little Burma Railways, which had functioned to the last and played a big part in evacuating many thousands of refugees and wounded soldiers in the path of the rapidly advancing Japanese.

definitions.definition: To make empty; to empty out; to remove the contents of, including to create a vacuum.

quote.citation: 1825, James Marsh, Preliminary Essay to Aids to Reflection:
quote.text: Evacuate the Scriptures of their most important doctrines.

definitions.definition: To remove; to eject; to void; to discharge, as the contents of a vessel, or of the bowels.

quote.citation: 1822, John Barclay, chapter I, in An Inquiry Into the Opinions, Ancient and Modern, Concerning Life and Organization‎[1], Edinburgh, London: Bell & Bradfute; Waugh & Innes; G. & W. B. Whittaker, section I, page 1:
quote.text: In the living state, the body is observed to receive aliment; to assimilate a part; to evacuate what is redundant or useless; [...]

definitions.definition: To make void; to nullify; to vacate.

quote.citation: 1622, Francis, Lord Verulam, Viscount St. Alban [i.e. Francis Bacon], The Historie of the Raigne of King Henry the Seventh, […], London:  […]  W[illiam] Stansby for Matthew Lownes, and William Barret, →OCLC:
quote.text: it would not evacuate a marriage after cohabitation and actual consummation
